item.title: Listen for the change in a piano rehearsal
item.summary: A pianist describes a rehearsal that changes what performers listen for.
item.transcript_text: Everyone watched my left hand in the last movement because it played the repeating rhythm. It sounded neat from my seat. Then the singer asked why the phrase seemed to stop just before every important word. From the back of the hall I could hear what she meant. We were treating each beat as a small arrival. I asked the players to keep the time but listen to the end of the sung line and aim across the bar. It felt less secure at first. We recorded both versions and invited someone who hadn't been at rehearsal to listen without the score. She could tell us where the sentence turned in the second version. That was enough to keep trying it. It didn't settle how fast we should play.

questions.prompt: What was wrong with the first version?
options: The coordination of beats disrupted the shape of the sung phrase
The singer did not know the words
The left hand could not keep the rhythm
The players ended in different places
questions.explanation: The beats sounded neat but obscured the longer phrase.

questions.prompt: Why does the pianist mention moving in the hall?
options: The pianist had changed instruments
The singer needed a different stage position
The score could only be read in the audience
The issue was easier to hear from a different position
questions.explanation: Moving back made the singer’s observation audible.

questions.prompt: What did the musicians keep while making the change?
options: The habit of watching the pianist
The speed as a settled decision
The timing of the beats
The same target inside each bar
questions.explanation: The players keep the time while aiming across the bar.

questions.prompt: What made the outside listener’s observation useful?
options: She knew which version was supposed to work
She followed a turn in meaning without seeing the written structure
She compared marks on the score
She had played in the first version
questions.explanation: The listener could locate the turn using only the sound.

options: The tempo
Whether to hear the singer
Whether to record two versions
Whether to play the last movement
questions.explanation: The pianist says the trial did not settle speed.
